newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ad industry growth weaker than world rate.
newsitem.headline: German ad industry growth weaker than world rate.

text.p: The German advertising industry's growth is being stifled by increasingly fierce competition in the world market, industry officials told reporters on Friday.

The president of the German Association of Advertising Agencies (GWA), Lothar Leonhard, said although the German industry had seen moderate growth last year, it paled in comparision to the worldwide boom, which was twice as strong.
Dynamic Asian markets have seen even faster expansion, Leonhard said. Because of this trend, he said, many large advertisers are investing abroad, rather than in Germany.

"Especially the Asian market is growing in unimaginable ways," Leonhard said. "Asia, Latin America, eastern Europe and the United States are the growth markets where industries are investing in marketing and advertising."

Leonhard gauged advertising investments overseen by ad agencies to be about 56 billion marks in 1996, a 4.5 percent rise from the previous year. He said over 55,000 brands are advertised in Germany, 3,000 of them on television.

He said the television market was experiencing what he called destructive price wars fueled by increasingly cut-throat competition for advertising. Leonhard warned however that the advertising industry should expect further price hikes.

Leonhard was speaking at a news conference about the Marketing Services fair, which will run from April 23-26 in Frankfurt. Organisers said they expect about 900 exhibitors, 75 of whom are from outside Germany, and about 20,000 visitors.

Marketing volume in Germany was estimated at 128 billion marks, up about seven percent from 1995, said Michael Peters, managing director of the Messe Frankfurt GmbH convention centre, which will host the marketing fair.
